description:
## What to remove

**`take_positive_step/2`** (`lib/enum.fz`) is a two-clause family with a `@spec` that nothing calls. `take_positive/2` inlines the same decision as an `if` inside a closure. The clause family is the shape the rest of the module uses; the closure is what actually runs.

**`Enum.slice/1`**, `fn slice(_enumerable), do: {:error, :unsupported}`, is a stray copy of the Enumerable protocol callback. That callback belongs to `Enumerable` and is implemented per type in `lib/enumerable.fz` -- List and Map answer it, Range answers it with a real slicing function. Nothing calls `Enum.slice/1`, and it occupies the name Elixir gives to `Enum.slice/2` and `Enum.slice/3`.

**`concat_list/2`** turned out to need deleting rather than renaming. It reads

```
fnp concat_list([], right), do: right
fnp concat_list([head | tail], right), do: [head | concat_list(tail, right)]
```

which is `List.concat/2` clause for clause. `Enum.concat/2` and `concat_list/1` already call `List.concat/2`; only `flat_map_list/2` called the copy. So the collision with `concat_list/1` (flatten one level) resolves by folding the duplicate away, and the surviving `concat_list` needs no new name.

## Acceptance

- Neither dead function remains, and no caller looked for them.
- One `concat_list` remains, and list append has one implementation.
- Gate green. Diagnostics goldens that quote `Enum.fz` line numbers re-blessed for drift; confirm digits-stripped equality before blessing.

comments.text: Done in 57a86546d. take_positive_step/2 and Enum.slice/1 deleted; concat_list/2 folded into List.concat/2 rather than renamed, since it was that function clause for clause. Every expected.txt unchanged including the allocation goldens; eight diagnostics goldens re-blessed for line drift, and enum_map_family loses exactly one warning -- the clause-coverage warning about concat_list/2. Gate green: lib 1978/0, matrix 642/0, aot 30/0, cli 225/0, doc, clippy, fmt.

title: Enum: delete the dead code and the duplicate helper name
